claim: STOCK Act (2012) requires members of Congress to disclose transactions over $1,000 within 30-45 days. Retail copy-trading platforms (Quiver Quantitative, Capitol Trades) aggregate these filings; Pelosi's disclosed portfolio returned 71% in 2024 vs the S&P 500's 25%. NANC (Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic ETF, Tidal Financial Group) is described as a regulated, exchange-listed fund mirroring Democratic members' disclosed trades.
quote: the market may have already partly priced in whatever information advantage the lawmaker held
limitations: Knowledge-hub summary, not a primary regulatory or academic source; no risk-adjusted performance figures.
independent_replication: No independent third-party backtest of a rotation mechanism across these 4 ETFs found in this or the prior gap-search round.
impact_on_spec: Grounds the POLITICAL menu's disclosure-replica-ETF story and the disclosure-lag caveat used in the stop condition; does not supply any rule parameter used by this batch (menu, grid and mechanism are this batch's own choice, reusing rotation_cell).

claim: Since the 2023-02-07 launch through 2026-04: NANC total return 88.49% (vs S&P 500's 74.70%, outperformed); GOP 64.31% (underperformed). NANC's top holdings are mega-cap tech (NVDA 9.0%, MSFT 7.6%, AMZN 5.2%, CRM 4.2%, GOOGL 3.9%). Explicit skeptical claim: outperformance was accidental, a byproduct of tech concentration rather than any genuine informational edge from tracking lawmakers; 45-day disclosure lag means holdings reflect past congressional decisions rather than real-time positioning; 0.74% expense ratio; regulatory risk from a proposed 2026-01 congressional stock-trading ban.
quote: was accidental, a byproduct of tech concentration
limitations: Simple since-inception total return, not annualized/risk-adjusted, not cost-adjusted beyond the fund's own expense ratio, single article's holdings snapshot (not point-in-time across the full period).
independent_replication: None found for a rotation-across-the-4-ETF-menu strategy specifically; the article covers each fund's own buy-and-hold-since-launch record only.
impact_on_spec: Directly motivates the PLACEBO_BIGTECH menu (QQQ/XLK/SPY/DIA) preregistered in candidate-manifest.json as the placebo-dominance disqualifier; the since-inception return numbers are NOT used as a target or backtest input by this batch (this batch computes its own return series from the local SIP panel independently).

claim: NANC is actively managed, not index-tracking: invests in securities that sitting Democratic members of Congress (or family) disclosed via STOCK Act Periodic Transaction Reports. Holdings weighted by reported trading intensity (recurring/large/multi-member purchases overweighted; small/stale/one-off trades excluded or underweighted). Typically holds 100-200 positions; TER 0.72%, non-diversified.
quote: Individual holdings are weighted based on the level of reported trading in a security by Democratic U.S. Congresspeople
limitations: Reached via WebSearch synthesis after a direct WebFetch to subversivetrading.com and subversiveetfs.com failed (DNS/network error in this sandboxed session); content corroborated by the same description on etf.com/NANC and mutualfunds.com in the same search result set.
independent_replication: Corroborated by TipRanks, Trackinsight and ETF.com fund pages surfaced in the same search.
impact_on_spec: Primary-source confirmation of the fund's actual construction rule (disclosure-weighted active management, not price momentum) -- underscores that this batch's rotation_cell mechanism (price-trend cross-sectional momentum ACROSS the 4 political ETFs) is a different, second-order mechanism layered on top of each fund's own first-order disclosure-replica construction, not a replication of the congressional-copy-trading edge itself.

claim: Capitol Losses: The Mediocre Performance of Congressional Stock Portfolios (Eggers and Hainmueller, Journal of Politics 2013): reconstructed actual member portfolios from financial disclosure forms (2004-2008), Fama-French 3-factor and Carhart 4-factor panel regressions. Finding: no evidence of informed trading or above-market returns for Congress as a whole or any identifiable subset of members; congressional portfolios under-performed a passive index fund by 2-3% per year over the sample.
quote: No evidence of either informed trading or above-market portfolio returns for Congress as a whole or any identifiable subset of members
limitations: Old sample (2004-2008), raw member portfolios (not these replica ETFs), no cross-sectional-momentum-rotation mechanism tested.
independent_replication: Cited widely in later congressional-trading literature (e.g. arXiv 2602.05514, Detecting Information Channels in Congressional Trading via Temporal Graph Learning) as the standard null-result reference; not independently re-run here.
impact_on_spec: Direct negative-evidence check on the congressional information edge story that motivates the POLITICAL menu; not on these specific ETFs (which launched 2017-2023) or this batch's rotation mechanism, so it does not by itself refute this candidate set, but grounds the requirement that any POLITICAL-menu edge found here be checked against the PLACEBO_BIGTECH menu before being attributed to the political-copy-trade framing.
